4.OVARIAN CYST IN POST-MENOPAUSAL WOMEN:
•Incidence of cyst = 5 –17% (simple cysts).
•Clinical presentation:
⇨Acute pain – cyst accident.
⇨Work – up of PMB.
⇨Incidental findings.
•Initial assessment by CA – 125 & TVS.

History:

•Risk factor of malignancy
•Symptoms of malignancy (same as in premenopausal).
•Family history of CA ovary, bowel and Breast.

Women is high risk of CA if she is 1st degree relative of Cancer Affected.

Significant family Hx:

1.> 2 cases of malignancy who r 1st degree relative of each other
2.1 case of CA ovary at any age +1 case of CA breast, <50years relative of each other’s.
3.1 case of CA ovary at any age + 2 cases of CA breast <60years relative of each other.
4.3 or more cases of CA colon

OR

2 CA colon + 1 CA stomach.

OR

2CA colon + 1 CA ovary.

OR

2 CA colon + 1 CA endometrium

OR

2 CA colon + 1 CA Bladder

5.1 individual with CA ovary + CA breast.

Referral to regional center for Genetic Services.

•IBS for 12m0 + Age >50years or Fx of CA => appropriate tests to rule out malignancy

Physical Examination:

•15 – 51% sensitivity.
•Ascites, + mass => urgent referral.

Tumor makers:

•CA – 125 – 78% Sensitivity & Specificity to differentiate between benign and malignant.
•HE4 – fewer false positive than CA – 125, not raised in Endometriosis.
•CEA
•CDx2
•Cancer Antigen 72 – 4.
•CA – 19- 9.
•αFP
•LDH
•B-HCG.

USG:

TVS = single most effective way.

TAS = Not used in isolation. Used as supplementary tool with TVS if mass is beyond the field of TVS.

•Description of cyst on TVS detailed features:
1.Simple:
-95 – 99% benign.
-Thin wall
-Post acoustic shadow.
-Anechoic fluid.
-Absence of septation or nodules, in multilocular
-Incomplete septation Papilla <3 cm.
2.Complex:
-Complete septation.
-Solid nodules.
-Papillary projection > 3cm.
1.In multilocular cyst risk of malignancy is 8%
2.In solid components 36 – 39%

Doppler – no used routinely.

Spectral/pulsed Doppler – not used routinely

3D USG – Not used routinely

Power Doppler – help to differentiate between benign and malignant by detecting blood flow in papilla centrally or solid components.

CT scan:

•Not used routinely as P0 tool.
•Suspicion of malignancy on the basis of clinical Picture, USG, and tumor, makers

CT scan of abdomen + pelvis to stage the disease. And to differentiate between P0 & II0 cancer

•Do oncology referral after CT scan.

MRI:

•Not used as P0 tool routinely.
•2nd line imaging for characterization of indeterminate ovarian cyst when USG is inconclusive.
•Contrast enhanced MRI has superior certainty.

PET – CT:

•No clear Advantage.

Scoring systems:

•RMI
•OVA 1: >4.4 high risk of malignancy.
•ROMA: CA – 125, HE4 and menopausal Status

> 2.27 => high risk of malignancy.

•IOTA: in Pre-Menopausal, overall IOTA has better linear regression .IOTA is better than RMI.
